title: "Is there an AI bubble?” Gavin Baker and David George
summary:
From capital allocation and infrastructure spending to business models and margins, it's
a detailed data-driven look at where we actually are in the AI cycle and what's likely to happen
next. But there's no debate that thus far the ROI on AI has been really positive and valuation
wise. And I think that is the mentality for sure at Google and perhaps meta.

reader_summary.headline: Gavin Baker argues there is no AI bubble because spending yields positive returns.
reader_summary.overview: Gavin Baker believes companies are not in an AI bubble because their spending on hardware generates positive returns. Unlike the 2000 dot-com bubble, today's AI tools are actively used and create value. Big tech firms have enough cash to fund these projects without causing a financial crash.

key_points.text: Companies spending on AI hardware see positive returns on investment so far.
key_points.evidence_quote: thus far, the ROI on all the spending has been really positive.

key_points.text: Today's AI hardware is actively used, unlike unused fiber cables in the 2000 bubble.
key_points.evidence_quote: Contrast that with today. There are no dark GPUs.

key_points.text: Big tech firms have $500 billion in cash, making a financial crash unlikely.
key_points.evidence_quote: They have $500 billion of cash on the balance sheet.

key_points.text: The early stage of AI is like the early internet, making it hard to predict winners.
key_points.evidence_quote: if we're going to make an analogy and say that chat GPT is to AI has Netscape Navigator was to the internet.

key_points.text: Software companies must accept lower profit margins as proof that customers use new AI features.
key_points.evidence_quote: It is definitely impossible, given what we just discussed, to succeed in AI without gross margin pressure.
